quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loose.
Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
To stop the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what lights should you use?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use parking lights only.
Use headlights only.
Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. Other drivers must be able to clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane road?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
When your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road if you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers from both directions can pass.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you must drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is a passing lane available and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a multilane road with multiple lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do if a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions when a crossing guard, sign, or law enforcement officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep a larger distance between you and other cars.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Visibility is lower at night. Take steps to make driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When a child is about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if a child starts to run into the street in front of you.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: What is a danger of driving much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It is very safe driving.
You always have the right-of-way.
You should not let other cars pass.
It may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be unsafe. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, carefully exit the road and turn on your hazard flashers. Park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to signal that your car is disabled.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross these lines to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always give way to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and safely pull to the right side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic and the emergency vehicle is directly behind you, keep moving slowly until you can get out of its way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Traffic regulation signs tell drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means you cannot make a right turn.

questions.question: You are in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Information signs about destinations are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What is a rule for drivers under 21 with a probationary license?

options.text: You may use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
You cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
You do not have to wear a seat belt.
You may use a hand-held cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses have certain rules. You cannot use any cell phone (hand-held or hands-free) and you must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Move out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up, as this may anger them and make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around there.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What does a green arrow displayed with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your lights to tell the aggressive driver he is wrong.
Take a driving action to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver may escalate the situation and increase danger.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a travel lane?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, go to the next one or where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: In what ways can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you a false sense of confidence.
It impairs your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time and impairs your coordination, balance, and vision. It also makes it hard to judge distance and react to your surroundings.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You can only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you not follow another car too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time to stop if the car in front of you stops or slows down quickly. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around the lowered gates.
Drive normally and assume no train is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be near. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: What happens when drivers drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They drive better because they are more careful.
They react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Slow down.
Follow the car ahead closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When it rains, slow down and turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower thinking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol damage your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm out?

options.text: Stop completely and wait to go.
Honk and pass on the left.
Drive when you think kids are done getting off.
Pass before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to go.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus's stop arm is out. Do not move until the arm is pulled in.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps you stay alert.
Yes, it is a distraction.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: A pedestrian steps in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Be extra careful around children.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra travel time.
Obey posted speed limits.
Use proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage becomes more common. To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave plenty of extra time for your trip.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may increase.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both may decrease.
Only the alcohol's effects may decrease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make the effects of both stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What can happen when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of both decrease.
The effects of both increase.
It will cure your illness.
It will improve your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. Driving after alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Driving after combining them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light signals.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help traffic flow and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic at that intersection.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always stop before a railroad crossing if flashing red lights are on, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close to the crossing. If you are unsure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers of an area with low clearance.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to these vehicles and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. Yield to drivers already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have room to merge safely.

questions.question: If you drive with a suspended license and cause an accident that injures someone, what happens?

options.text: You will receive a warning.
You will only pay a fine.
You may pay a fine, have your suspension extended, and go to jail.
You will receive points on your license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pay a fine, have your suspension extended, and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving with a suspended license is illegal. You will be fined, may go to jail for up to 45 days, and will have your license suspension extended.
